tools.name: interpret_requirement
tools.description: Give Aseptway the buyer's requirement, or a correction or addition to it, in their own words: it is read into a structured requirement (each value says which words it came from), conflicting or unclear facts come back as one question, and words not yet read are kept as written. tools.name: get_requirement
tools.description: A Aseptway requirement as it stands: each value with where it came from, what it replaced, the open question, words not yet read, whether it was sent and any offer on it.

tools.name: edit_requirement
tools.description: Set fields by name ({"op":"set","values":{...}}, an empty value clears) or change the list ({"op":"add"|"update"|"remove"|"replace", ...}), exactly as given: no reading. Use it to answer the open question when the answer is a value.

tools.name: send_requirement
tools.description: Send the requirement to Aseptway once the buyer says to: the first send records the request (its receipt token is the requirement's token, for request_status and offers); a later send of a changed requirement records a revision of the same request. tools.name: request_status
tools.description: Resume a requirement using the receipt credentials. Read the recorded requirement, any replies the business has published on it (messages: where it answers a buyer with no email, it answers here) and any linked offers. Answer a reply by sending a continuation. Contact details are kept apart.

tools.name: accept_offer
tools.description: Place an order on terms you have inspected and the buyer has authorized you to accept. Requires the exact terms hash and explicit acceptance. Follow inspect_offer later for payment links and verified payment state.

tools.name: decline_offer
tools.description: Decline an issued offer on its inspected terms.

tools.name: release_payment
tools.description: Confirm a payment condition only where the inspected order allows the customer to release it. This records approval; it does not pay the processor.

tools.name: retrieve_deliverable
tools.description: Retrieve what a paid order delivers, where the business produces it itself (a report): the exact text, its SHA-256, version, sources and any shortfall. Before payment is confirmed it says it is not yet available. Use the offer link or linked request credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: submit_request, request_status, inspect_offer, counter_offer · Private data: submit_request, interpret_requirement, send_requirement, request_status, inspect_offer, release_payment, retrieve_deliverable, state_purchasing_requirements, report_vendor_status, inspect_delivery, answer_remedy · Public sink: submit_request, send_requirement, request_status, submit_purchase_order · Destructive: submit_request, edit_requirement.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: submit_request, request_status, inspect_offer, counter_offer · Private data: submit_request, interpret_requirement, send_requirement, request_status, inspect_offer, release_payment, retrieve_deliverable, state_purchasing_requirements, report_vendor_status, inspect_delivery, answer_remedy · Public sink: submit_request, send_requirement, request_status, submit_purchase_order · Destructive: submit_request, edit_requirement

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
